devMemory.summary: A/B measurement of B-cee5 prompt stopgap: agents deviate from scan mandates either way, and no mechanical read-evidence exists to detect it.
devMemory.lesson: Old full-scan prompt: the agent silently disobeyed (read 1 of 111 decisions docs, no audit trail) yet asserted complete coverage — in production such deviation is invisible, so coverage claims under the old prompt were unverifiable; when agents DO obey, the 2.4MB corpus costs ~600k+ input tokens (the original exhaustion). New bounded contract produced equivalent review quality (same load-bearing gaps and same spec-contradiction OQ) at 74.8k vs 79.3k tokens with a recorded enumeration + candidate basis + explicit non-escalation reason. Core gap remaining: what a reviewer actually READ is self-reported prose, not evidence — there is no read manifest bound to scope_check_save/review_pass_set and no transcript-derived read log, so future before/after comparisons and compliance proofs (detecting unrecorded full scans) have no ground truth. Prompt-layer stopgap is instructional only; proof needs mechanical read evidence.
devMemory.reusePrompt: reviewer read evidence, scan compliance, token stopgap measurement, read manifest, scanEscalationReason audit, B-cee5 effect

devMemory.summary: A story whose diff includes package.json turns every later main merge into related drift: quorum, delivery-check, and review passes all stale and force a full re-review round.
devMemory.lesson: storyFilesHash covers the story diff file set. package.json is in that set whenever the story wires npm scripts (or gets scope-acknowledged version bumps), and DONE auto-bumps touch package.json on every merge to main — so any sibling story landing first changes YOUR story-owned material. Cost in B-3b05: one extra TEST->DEV->REVIEW round (4 reviewer lanes re-pass), fresh quorum_submit, fresh delivery_check_set. Mitigations: close stories promptly once quorum is bound; expect and budget the round-4 re-review when parallel stories share package.json; command-backed evidence must be actually re-run (refresh_stale refuses to rebind it silently).
devMemory.reusePrompt: stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch after merge / review assurance floor local rounds 0 after mergeMain / related drift package.json

devMemory.summary: Run quorum_submit during REVIEW, before advancing to TEST, once all active lanes have current-round passes.
devMemory.lesson: quorum_submit satisfies the 3x2 review-assurance floor by converting CURRENT-round signed review passes from ALL active reviewer lanes into host verdict records (hostA=claude-cli hostB=codex-cli); it refuses to fabricate. review_run_start/review_pass_set are REVIEW-phase-only, so advancing to TEST first (the round-2+ gate needs only >=1 receipt) strands the other lanes without a write path and forces a TEST->DEV->REVIEW round-trip to mint fresh passes in a new round. Correct order: all lanes pass in current round -> quorum_submit -> story_advance TEST.
devMemory.reusePrompt: review assurance floor blocked / quorum_submit missing current pass lanes / review_pass_set not available in TEST

devMemory.summary: Byte-budget assertions over output containing live machine state are nondeterministic; disable environment-dependent sections in fixtures via their documented env switches.
devMemory.lesson: The doctor brief includes the advisory host burn scan which streams the operator live ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions state, so the smoke byte count varied with session activity (B-fa65 F-004: 20239 then 20606 on identical code). Fix pattern: the fixture invocations set LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0 (the scan documented disable switch) on every doctor call so the budget asserts the projection deterministically; the budget value itself stays untouched. Generalization: grep the feature for an env disable switch before patching budgets or output.
devMemory.reusePrompt: doctor brief under budget got NNNNN / brief-output-smoke nondeterministic / burn scan bytes vary

devMemory.summary: Parallel reviewers' destructive dist bite-tests on a shared story worktree race each other; serialize them or use an isolated worktree copy.
devMemory.lesson: Destructive compiled-dist experiments (remove a registry name, run smoke, restore) must not overlap other reviewers using the same dist: a concurrently patched dist yields spurious FAIL observations. Either serialize the destructive step after all read-only lanes finish, or do what the round-2 quality lane did: build a scratch git worktree copy and bite there. Byte-restore and re-run the smoke afterward to prove the shared dist is intact.
devMemory.reusePrompt: dist bite test race, shared worktree destructive experiment, spurious smoke failure during review
